title: Mother of God (Council of Ephesus, 431)
hook: the crowds in Ephesus cheered when the council called Mary God-bearer, a claim about who Jesus is

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Immaculate Conception: Mary's own beginning, kept free of original sin. Your line was prepared from the start. What did you prepare for someone? Day eighty.

Summer, in the year 431, in the city of Ephesus, on the coast of what's now Turkey. Around two hundred bishops have gathered in a church dedicated to Mary. The whole city is waiting outside. They've been arguing for months about one word, a word ordinary people used in their prayers. Late in the evening the decision comes out, and the crowd goes wild. People light torches and walk the bishops back to their lodgings, singing, with incense burning in the streets. All over one word, a title for a mother that was really a claim about her son. Today's word is that title.
screen: `EPHESUS, 431.` → `TWO HUNDRED BISHOPS, ONE WORD.` → `TORCHES IN THE STREETS.`

segments.voice: Theotokos. Greek. Theos, God, and tokos, giving birth. God-bearer. Or, as it's usually put in English, Mother of God. Christians had been calling Mary this for a long time. But Nestorius, the archbishop of Constantinople, was uneasy. Surely, he said, Mary gave birth to the human Jesus, not to God. Better to call her Christ-bearer. It sounds careful. But Cyril, the bishop of Alexandria, argued that it led somewhere dangerous: to splitting Jesus into two, a man who was born and a God who was not. The council sided with Cyril. Its teaching: Jesus isn't two people sharing a body. He's one person, truly God and truly human. So the one Mary carried and nursed and taught to walk is God the Son, and she is truly the mother of God. That's why today's line is a claim about her son. Theotokos protects the truth about Jesus first. It doesn't mean Mary is older than God, or the source of God. For the council, it means the baby in her arms was God made man. Catholics hear the idea already in Elizabeth's greeting, in the Douay-Rheims: "And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?" Catholics say the title every time they pray the Hail Mary: "Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen." And the Church begins every new year with it: January first is the Solemnity of Mary, the Mother of God. Orthodox Christians use the Greek word itself in their liturgy.
screen: `THEOS AND TOKOS: GOD-BEARER.` · `NOT JUST CHRIST-BEARER.` · `ONE PERSON, GOD AND MAN.` · `JANUARY FIRST, EVERY YEAR.` · then, large: `THE MOTHER OF MY LORD.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: one Hail Mary, slowly. Settle and breathe. If you pray, say the Hail Mary once, so slowly that each phrase gets a breath of its own. When you reach Mother of God, stop for a moment and let the claim land: the one she held, Catholics say, was God. Then finish, and sit in the quiet. If you don't pray, you can just hear the words in your mind and notice what they're claiming. Either way, no rush. The bell holds the time.
Theotokos. Greek for God-bearer: Mary, Mother of God, a title that is first of all a claim about who her son is. Today's word.
Your line: a claim about her son. Today, when you hear someone honored, notice what the honor says about the people around them. Day eighty.

howItsDone: Catholics call Mary Mother of God in every Hail Mary and celebrate the Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God, on 1 January; Orthodox Christians call her Theotokos throughout their liturgy.

fork.setup: you're at Ephesus in 431. an archbishop says Mary should only be called Christ-bearer, not God-bearer. what does the council say?
options: God-bearer: her son is one person, truly God and truly man.
fork.reveal: the council affirmed Theotokos, God-bearer, because Jesus is one person, not two, and the crowds outside celebrated with torches.

original.note: Greek: God-bearer, the one who gave birth to God. affirmed at Ephesus in 431.

trapdoor: what you thought: Mother of God is a title of honor for Mary.
what it means: it's first a claim about Jesus: one person, truly God and truly man, so his mother is the mother of God.
what a scholar hears: Theotokos against Christotokos, Cyril against Nestorius, Ephesus 431. and the word was already in Christian prayer before the council met.

notes: Douay-Rheims wording of Luke 1:43 given from memory; confirm.
Council of Ephesus met June–July 431 in the Church of Mary; roughly 150–200 bishops (counts vary). Confirm 'around two hundred'.
The torchlight procession is described in a letter of Cyril of Alexandria to his church (often numbered Letter 24). Confirm the reference.
Nestorius's position summarized fairly? He preferred Christotokos; modern scholars debate how 'Nestorian' Nestorius was. Keeper may want a softer phrasing.
'Already in Christian prayer before the council': the Sub tuum praesidium (papyrus variously dated 3rd–4th century) and earlier Fathers (e.g. Alexander of Alexandria). Confirm.
Solemnity of Mary, Mother of God on 1 January. Confirm.
Hail Mary cited in its traditional English form, as on other Catholic days.

'Around two hundred bishops' rests on Cyril's letter; Keeper to confirm the count there.
